author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows, by stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it by full name, on one page. It is reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, all on one page with no pagination.
Under each specialty, every veterinarian holding it is listed by full name, first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page.
A veterinarian holding several specialties appears under each of them (edge case 1).
A specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian under it (edge case 2).
Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order (edge case 3).
Specialty names render as stored in every language; the page's own wording is present in every supported language and none is hard-coded (edge case 4; REQ-LANG-002).
The page carries the standard navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory (REQ-SYS-001); no page, navigation included, links to the specialty directory.
The page offers no way to add, change, or remove a veterinarian or a specialty (edge case 5; NG-2).
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties (NG-2, unchanged by owner decision).
Any navigation entry or link from another page to the specialty directory; the owner deferred a visible entry point to a follow-up request.
Listing veterinarians who hold no specialty.
Searching or filtering specialties or veterinarians (NG-9).
notes: Scope grounded in intake-decision line 1: 'A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; ... (non-goal NG-2 is unchanged)' and 'The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link from another page is part of this request.' No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. Narrowest readings taken per the request and recorded as PRD Open Questions: (1) order is required only to be stable, with the specific order left to design; (2) an unheld specialty is listed with no veterinarian under it and no explicit 'none' marker; (3) the visible entry point is deferred. The ubiquitous language is unchanged: Specialty and Veterinarian already cover the terms. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Read-only inverse view inside the existing vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure, § Contracts). It uses in-force patterns only (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog). A Repository per persisted lookup type, like PetTypeRepository, adds SpecialtyRepository. That is required because unheld specialties (edge case 2) cannot be derived from vets. A Value object, SpecialtyDirectory, does the grouping and ordering without I/O. A Web controller, SpecialtyController, binds nothing, delegates, and selects the view. A Thymeleaf template goes under templates/vets/. Specialty gains no inverse association: the Vet-owned @ManyToMany and the /vets serialization stay unchanged. Adjustments written to docs/system-design.md: three Contracts rows plus REQ-VET-003 on Vet, Specialty, and VetRepository; the vet/ package line; the invariants paragraph (grouping by specialty identity; order specialties by name then id, holders by last name, first name, then id; no link to the page); and a new § Scale and Load section with the specialty-directory row. Stable order: the PRD leaves the specific order to design, and the design resolves it as stated. Grep-based basis (IDE oracle not connected): VetRepository.findAll() is @Cacheable("vets"); Vet.getSpecialties() sorts by name; NamedEntity/BaseEntity override no equals/hashCode; layout fragment signature is layout(template, menu); message keys 'specialties' and 'name' already exist.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html (SpecialtyController): binds no request parameter, path variable, or model attribute, so it has no binding target and no persisted type is bound. Locale switching stays with the global WebConfiguration interceptor. No pagination parameter is accepted (product decision).

Double, pure core: SpecialtyDirectoryTests builds real Vet and Specialty instances in memory with no double. Most acceptance criteria and edge cases 1-3 are asserted here: several specialties per vet, unheld specialty, vet with none, stable order, and distinct Specialty instances sharing one id.
Double, framework transport: SpecialtyControllerTests uses MockMvc (@WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class)), the sanctioned transport stand-in (testing-principles § Mocking Policy).

Double, repository boundary in the web test: hand-written in-memory implementations of VetRepository and SpecialtyRepository registered as beans through a nested @TestConfiguration. A @MockitoBean stub is not sanctioned for the new test; the existing VetControllerTests stub is tolerated as is.

Double, persistence: none. The real H2 seed is exercised through the existing @SpringBootTest seam (PetClinicIntegrationTests) or a @DataJpaTest, confirming SpecialtyRepository returns all seeded specialties, including over the real vet cache.

Template: vets/specialtyList.html uses the layout fragment with a menu key that matches no navigation item, so the standard navigation renders (REQ-SYS-001) with nothing highlighted and no entry added. The heading and labels reuse existing message keys ('specialties', 'vets'/'name') where they fit. Any new key lands in all bundles, which I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces (REQ-LANG-002). Specialty names and veterinarian full names render through th:text.

No-link criterion (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldNotBeLinkedFromNavigation): assert that no template under src/main/resources/templates references the /specialties.html route. Walk the templates the same way I18nPropertiesSyncTest walks resources. Optionally also check that the rendered welcome and vet pages carry no such href.

patterns.description: Repository for a persisted lookup value; SpecialtyRepository mirrors it read-only (extend Repository<Specialty,Integer>, @Transactional(readOnly = true) on findAll, as VetRepository does). The directory owns the ordering, so no ORDER BY is required.
Constructor-injected repositories, @GetMapping on a .html route returning a view name under vets/; SpecialtyController follows this shape minus pagination.
Full-name rendering as firstName + ' ' + lastName and escaped th:text output. In SpecialtyDirectory the composition moves into the value object, so the template renders plain strings.

risks.risk: Specialty instances from SpecialtyRepository and those inside cached Vet objects are distinct, and NamedEntity defines no equals/hashCode. Grouping by instance or by Set membership silently drops every holder.
risks.mitigation: Group by specialty id (system-design § Contracts invariants paragraph); a SpecialtyDirectoryTests case uses two Specialty instances with the same id.

risks.risk: Specialty directory path scales with specialties x holdings (system-design § Scale and Load, specialty-directory row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form per the row: one pass into a map keyed by specialty id, then standard-library sorts. No pagination and no hand-written structure.

risks.risk: Stable order across equal names: the schema indexes specialties.name without a uniqueness constraint, and veterinarian names can repeat.
risks.mitigation: Comparator chains end in identity: specialties by name then id, holders by last name, first name, then id (system-design § Contracts invariants paragraph).

risks.risk: Stored names rendered into HTML (system-design § Threat Model, cross-site scripting row).
risks.mitigation: th:text only, never th:utext. Names are seeded with no write path (NG-2), and escaping stays the default control (security-principles).

risks.risk: Business rule drifting into the controller (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row; § Design Validation Checklist).
risks.mitigation: Grouping, full-name composition, and ordering live in SpecialtyDirectory. The controller reads two repositories, builds the directory, adds it to the model, and returns the view name.

risks.risk: Mixed freshness: the vet cache has no eviction while specialties are read fresh (system-design § Open Questions from the Survey, item 5).
risks.mitigation: Accepted as the existing cache posture: vet data changes only out of band. A specialty added out of band shows as unheld until the cache refreshes. No eviction work in this slice.
GET mapping only; no form, POST handler, or edit link in the template; SpecialtyRepository exposes no save or delete.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped. No ADR: the choices are contained to this slice and follow in-force catalog patterns (adr-template § When to Create an ADR). Open questions recorded rather than answered: (1) The specific order is a design resolution of the PRD open question, not a product decision. The product owner may later prefer a different holder order, such as by displayed full name; the change is one comparator in SpecialtyDirectory. (2) Whether an unheld specialty says 'none' stays open in the PRD; as scoped, it renders with an empty holder list and no marker. (3) The term 'specialty directory' comes from the PRD and is not in docs/ubiquitous-language.md. This triage is not foundational, so that file is outside its write scope; the product-requirements-expert may add the term. (4) docs/system-design.md lacked a § Scale and Load section; this dispatch added it with the harness template's comment and the one row this slice needs.

Shared cached state is not mutated: SpecialtyDirectory.of reads the cached VetRepository.findAll() collection and Vet.getSpecialties() (Vet.java:60-63 returns a freshly collected sorted list). Surface widening is stated and bounded: one new read-only GET page with no pagination, sized in system-design.md § Scale and Load as bounded, over data the /vets route already exposes in full. It exposes no new data class and does not change management exposure.
